claim: Most existing LLM-IRT evaluation work uses only standard unidimensional item response models (1PL/2PL/3PL) that treat benchmark items as independent; hierarchical, nested, and polytomous response models remain largely unexplored despite being the natural fit for grouped/testlet item structures.
stance_target: open methodological gap for testlet/nested IRT applied to multi-unit-test code benchmark tasks
scope_conditions: systematic review of 400+ LLM psychometrics references, as of 2025-2026
quoted_support: Most work to date uses standard IRT models (1PL, 2PL, 3PL), with little exploration of polytomous, hierarchical, or fully multidimensional models, despite the complexity of LLM capabilities.

claim: LLM Psychometrics is framed by this review as an emerging interdisciplinary field applying psychometric instruments and theory (validity, reliability, IRT) to LLM evaluation, benchmarking design, and capability enhancement.
stance_target: framing/positioning of psychometric approaches to LLM benchmark evaluation
quoted_support: This review paper introduces and synthesizes the emerging interdisciplinary field of LLM Psychometrics, which leverages psychometric instruments, theories, and principles to evaluate, understand, and enhance LLMs.
